Five days, five stories that moved a border, a coastline, or a front line: a strait, a stadium banner, a fence, a fleet and a frontier.

How the map moved this week — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ US and Iran traded strikes for a 5th straight day. The US reimposed a naval blockade and hit Greater Tunb Island — a strait islet Iran and the UAE have disputed for decades. Trump floated, then dropped, a 20% ship toll on the strait.

2/ Argentina beat England 2-1 in the World Cup semis, then unfurled a banner: "Las Malvinas son Argentinas." FIFA bans political messages — Argentina may face discipline over a 44-year-old sovereignty dispute reopened in seconds.

3/ Gibraltar and Spain marked their new border deal with a midnight ceremony — crowds crossed without checks for the first time. The line dates to 1713; Spain sealed it as recently as 1969-1985 under Franco.

4/ Zelenskyy dismissed defence minister Fedorov, architect of Ukraine's drone program, in a reshuffle. Days later Ukraine hit ~20 Russian vessels and Black Sea oil tankers, escalating its campaign to cut Crimea's supply lines.

5/ India is stepping up removals of alleged Bangladeshi migrants; Bangladesh is pushing back, leaving people stranded at the frontier. The 4,000km+ border was drawn hastily in 1947 and has rarely been fully settled since.

The data behind it: Ukraine spends 40%+ of GDP on defence — the darkest shade on this map, unmatched anywhere. Russia isn't far behind, and the Gulf states glow orange amid the Iran war. Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)
